title: RICE+OCI hybrid: prioritizing runtime feature work vs platform investments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: provide a reproducible, pragmatic prioritization framework that extends RICE with an Opportunity Cost Index (OCI) and an Operational Burden factor so PMs can compare small high-impact runtime experiments against larger platform investments (Dedicated/Private). This ticket captures the framework, worked examples, scoring spreadsheet references, and rollout guidance for planning cycles and OKRs.
background: We already use RICE variants for feature scoring, but infra/platform proposals (Dedicated capacity investments, Private deployment work, or major runtime re-architecture) often lose to product-surface features because reach/impact is estimated differently. Engineering and finance ask for clearer trade-offs that include ongoing unit-cost savings and failure-domain reduction. This hybrid model makes those trade-offs explicit.
framework_summary:
RICE+OCI hybrid (flat fields):
- Reach: weekly affected requests/users (normalized score)
- Impact: qualitative magnitude on key OKRs (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3)
- Confidence: percent estimate of the scores' accuracy
- Effort: dev+infra+design FTE-weeks, converted to points
- Opportunity Cost Index (OCI): present-value estimate of ongoing cost delta + risk-adjusted outage exposure (USD per month -> normalized score)
- Operational Burden (OB): expected ongoing SRE/ops maintenance in FTE-weeks per quarter (lower is better)
Scoring: Final score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence / Effort) * (1 + OCI_weight * normalized_OCI) * (1 - OB_weight * normalized_OB). Default OCI_weight=0.6, OB_weight=0.4. Normalize OCI and OB across candidate set using min-max to 0..1.
Rationale: keeps RICE signal while explicitly valuing recurring cost savings and reliability improvements from platform work.
scoring_steps:
1) Collect metrics: historical request volume, dollar-per-token cost by route, incident MTTD/MTTR impact, current ops load.
2) Estimate Reach (users/requests/week) and Impact (OKR delta) with product+eng input.
3) Estimate Effort (FTE-weeks) with ENG leads.
4) Calculate OCI: (expected monthly $ saved * 12)/discount_factor + expected avoided incident cost (probability * impact).
5) Compute normalized OCI and OB across candidates.
6) Apply weights and compute final rank.
7) Run sensitivity analysis on OCI_weight and OB_weight in +/−0.2 increments.
8) Present top-ranked candidates to GTM and Finance for alignment.
worked_examples:
Example A: Dynamic KV cache improvements (runtime micro-optimization)
- Reach: 200k requests/week
- Impact: 1.0 (improves latency for critical user flows)
- Confidence: 0.7
- Effort: 3 FTE-weeks
- OCI raw: estimated $10k/month savings + 30% reduction in high-sev incidents (~$6k/month expected avoided cost) => $16k/month -> normalized OCI 0.45
- OB: 0.1 FTE-wk/qtr -> normalized OB 0.05
- Final rank: high (favored: low effort, immediate cost savings)

Example B: Dedicated GPU pool expansion (platform)
- Reach: 10M requests/week (supports scale and new enterprise contracts)
- Impact: 2.0 (enables SLA-backed customers)
- Confidence: 0.6
- Effort: 24 FTE-weeks
- OCI raw: $60k/month (reduced external burst costs & higher committed revenue) -> normalized OCI 0.9
- OB: 1.2 FTE-wk/qtr -> normalized OB 0.5
- Final rank: competitive when OCI_weight is high; may lose in pure RICE but wins when OCI weighted >=0.5
acceptance_criteria:
- Framework documented in Confluence with formulas and worked examples.
- Scoring spreadsheet uploaded and linked.
- Two roadmap decisions (one runtime, one platform) scored using the framework and sensitivity analysis completed.
- Prioritization reviewed and signed off by ENG lead, Finance, and Head of Product.
- Playbook internal doc for PMs created explaining when to emphasize OCI vs classic RICE.
implementation_plan: 1) Draft confluence doc (this ticket). 2) Pull metric exports (usage, cost per route) — action ENG-analytics. 3) Run a pilot on the upcoming cycle candidates (Cycle 2026-W12). 4) Review pilot findings at Roadmap sync (week 2). 5) Iterate weights, publish final playbook.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: OCI estimates are noisy and can bias toward long-term infra. Mitigation: require a 3rd-party validation from Finance for OCI> $25k/month and run sensitivity banding.
Risk: Managers may manipulate Reach/Impact. Mitigation: require source links for Reach (metrics query) and impact tie to an explicit OKR.
Risk: OB underestimation. Mitigation: SRE must provide a conservative lower bound and we use the higher of PM/ENG/SRE estimates.
